scope: Read-only comparison of identical uncommitted current-sass-tool-references.mjs diffs in 21.x and main. No runtime, source profile or producer run.
verdict: No concrete blocker identified in API source under the stated batch and callback-sampling contracts. Real tests and attribution remain required.
observations: Original successful qualify/predecessor/comparison still execute the same core fresh member, input check and full bound physical sweep; unknown side returns null without reader callback or sweep as before.

Batch captures the complete input with plain before callbacks; plain rejects proxy, custom prototype, non-data/non-enumerable properties, symbol keys and malformed/sparse arrays. Exact request keys, permitted kind and metadata are validated before callbacks.

Before each request and after all callbacks plain(input) is compared with initial snapshot. Thus a later callback leaving a prior request changed is rejected; no result array is returned early. Each owned request runs core with a separate genuine member physical/provided/physical and current-after check; no callback/result reuse.

Full physical bound sweeps precede requests and follow all callbacks. The batch flag is checked by batch entry and actual guard preflight/consume/direct entry; try/finally releases it on exceptions. Other individual side calls remain callable during batching and keep their original sweeps.

Batch is intentionally stricter than isolated side calls for unknown requests, since it does full pre/final physical checks even for null results. Early validation, cold preflight and shared physical boundaries also change callback and failure ordering. These are additive API semantics, not exact arbitrary-reader call trace equivalence.
limits: Cross-request temporary mutation that is fully restored before next check is not continuously observed, matching stated contract.

Unrecognized data in reference objects remains accepted by existing metadata and preserved by plain/side; request object keys are strictly kind/reference. Comparison produces detached historical Buffer copies.
No frozen result requirement was specified; consumers should not use returned mutable objects or buffers as cached guard results or source authority.

Tests must establish direct, alternate scheduler and caught nested reentry; duplicate requests; forged/old/new callback path; prior request mutation; null/throw behavior; malformed proxy/accessor input; exception recovery; and real table integration without bypassing repairs/frames.
Finite source profile and pins currently stale; no source, runtime or owner qualification inferred.
